anchors: A step that collects every item before acting, or bounds memory only with a count limit, is a defect
decision: Self-Review item 7: for every caller-sized input the plan states held-per-item, growth and peak, prescribes a peak-memory test at two sizes (child max RSS where native code allocates, spool bytes where a spool exists), treats collect-then-act or a count-only bound as a defect, and allows a whole output only behind a byte limit.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for memory in this skill. GREEN probes on opus and haiku failed a read-everything-into-a-list import task and rewrote it as check pass plus action pass with a two-size peak test, quoting item 7.

reopen_if: Plans that pass this item still ship code whose peak memory grows with the input.
why: A plan is the last point where the data structure is cheap to change; a structure the tasks build on is a rewrite at review.

decision: Item 7 gives no numbers for N, the per-item byte limit, the two test sizes or the tolerance for not scaling.

evidence.text: Raised as a gap by every GREEN probe; declined as a per-project choice.

reopen_if: Plans repeatedly pick sizes too close together to show scaling.
why: Each depends on the project's data and host; a fixed number would be copied where it does not fit. The item requires the plan to state them.

anchors: A milestone label goes in the name after the colon
decision: Task ids start with a digit; a milestone label goes in the name after the colon, never in the id.

evidence.text: task_brief.py on a plan with '### Task M2.1:' headings exits 1 'the plan has no Task <id> headings at all'; '### Task 2.1: M2 parser' extracts (rc 0).

why: task_brief.py finds tasks by 'Task <digits>'; a plan headed '### Task M2.1:' is reported as having no task headings, and a three-altitude plan labels tasks by milestone naturally.

anchors: A task adds only the imports its own code uses
extract each task's blocks into a scratch copy of the repo in task order
A test that isolates `HOME` also sets `USERPROFILE`
check each DETAILED step's code against every behavioural sentence the MID plan states
decision: Self-Review items 8-11: each task imports, collects and lints on its own; the plan's code is extracted and run, its mutation battery included, and a substring assertion must fail with the guarded code deleted; platform claims agree with the CI OS matrix and HOME isolation also sets USERPROFILE; DETAILED code is checked against the MID plan's behavioural sentences.

evidence.text: Pre-edit text check: 0 hits for USERPROFILE, OS matrix, import-mode, mutation, extract. GREEN on opus and haiku: a seeded plan with M-ids, a forward import block, an importlib helper, Linux-only vs a 3-OS matrix, HOME-only isolation, an unrun battery, a substring assertion and continue-vs-break against the MID text; both tiers found each and quoted the deciding item.

reopen_if: Plans that pass items 8-11 still ship tasks that fail collection, a surviving battery arm, a platform-only test, or code contradicting the MID plan.
why: Each defect was found only by an implementer, a reviewer or CI after the plan was committed, costing fix rounds or a re-release; a read-only self-review cannot see them.

anchors: its code reads first and classifies the error (missing versus unreadable)
decision: Self-review item 14: code that must refuse over input it could not read reads first and classifies the error, never gating the read on Path.exists() or is_file(), and the plan prescribes a mode-000 RED test.

evidence.text: Ran Path.exists/is_file on a file inside a mode-000 directory as a non-root user: 3.12.15 and 3.13.16 raise PermissionError, 3.14.8 returns False for both.

reopen_if: The supported Python floor and behaviour change so that existence probes raise again on a permission error.
why: From Python 3.14 exists() and is_file() return False on a permission error (3.12 and 3.13 raise), so an unreadable directory reads as absent and the run reports success.

anchors: this task's code absent: it must fail there
decision: Each prescribed refusal test is run against the scratch copy with the earlier tasks applied and the task's own code absent, and must fail there.

evidence.text: Pre-edit probes (opus, haiku) answered NONE and named items 9 and 12 as too narrow; edited-text probes quoted item 14.

reopen_if: Plans routinely carry no extractable code, so the before-code run cannot be performed during self-review.
why: An earlier generic guard refusing the same verb or input makes a refusal test pass before any implementation, so it proves nothing about the new refusal; items 9 and 12 stated this only for substring assertions and argparse exit 2.

anchors: A check that refuses past a cap (a size, a count) stops reading the input as soon as the cap is passed
decision: Self-Review item 7 bounds TIME as well as memory: a check that refuses past a cap stops reading the input as soon as the cap is passed, and the plan prescribes a counting-generator test asserting the items read stop at the cap plus one.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a renderer size check walked a whole run first, so a confirmed count far past the cap held a worker for about 35 minutes before refusing while the memory test passed. Quote-back probe on opus and haiku found the rule only in the edited text.

reopen_if: Self-Review gains a separate cost or complexity item that covers caps.
why: A check that walks the whole caller-sized input before comparing is unbounded CPU while memory stays flat, so the memory test passes it.

anchors: Prove it by rebuilding each task's state alone
decision: Self-Review item 8 is proved by rebuilding each task's state alone (later tasks' additions removed) and running lint, format check, type check and that task's tests there, above all where one file is split across tasks.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a file split between two tasks passed the whole-tree gate and only a rebuild of the earlier task's state found a trailing-newline format error.

reopen_if: A tool rebuilds and gates each task's state automatically.
why: A whole-tree gate with every task applied cannot see a defect only the earlier state has.

anchors: names only the test files and test functions that exist once that task is applied
decision: A mutation battery split per task names only the test files and test functions that exist once that task is applied.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a task's battery named the next task's test file and had to be split in two.

reopen_if: Batteries are no longer split per task.
why: An arm relying on a later task's test file rests its RED on a file the implementer has not written yet.

decision: A scratch copy run on the main checkout's virtualenv with an editable install sets PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/src for tools that import the package, and confirms the imported module's __file__.

evidence.text: A queued incident: lint-imports passed against the main tree until PYTHONPATH pointed at the scratch src.

reopen_if: The extraction step always builds a fresh virtualenv for the scratch copy.
why: The editable install points imports at the main checkout's source, so import-linter (and pytest without a pythonpath setting) checks the wrong tree and passes.

anchors: run the formatter check over the plan FILE too
decision: Where the repo's gate formats Markdown code blocks, the formatter check also runs over the plan file itself.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a long plan passed every per-task check, then the main gate dedented a class-body fragment block and the format check failed.

reopen_if: The repo's gate stops formatting Markdown code blocks.
why: Extracting the code leaves the plan's fenced blocks unchecked, and the formatter rewrites an indented fragment block the first time the real gate runs.

anchors: ends with a task that writes its changelog entry under the repo's unreleased heading
decision: A plan for a user-visible change ends with a task that writes its changelog entry, checked against what the finished feature prints.

evidence.text: A queued incident: a whole feature with a new command landed with no changelog entry, found only by chance before a release.

reopen_if: The execution skill makes the controller write the changelog after the last task.
why: Each other task's brief covers its own code, so without a task of its own the entry is nobody's step.
